A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ZINA and VisionHall. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original VisionHall annotations, detection and editing results, qualitative examples, and decoupling, backbone and few-shot ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds external-benchmark evaluations, additional baseline comparisons, pruning ablations and dataset analyses.

M1.justification: The detector, deterministic tagging function, reviewer, Qwen2.5-VL-72B backbone and cross-entropy objectives remain unchanged. Error insertion and DAG-based augmentation also remain; their full synthetic-data prompts are unchanged apart from formatting. Expanded dependency explanations and newly disclosed pruning probability do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates on VisionHall. v2 additionally evaluates on MHaluBench's Image-to-Text subset and HalLoc, introducing external data with coarse claim/segment annotations and a different four-category localization benchmark (Table 4 and Appendix F.3). VisionHall coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The original VisionHall comparator set remains. v2 adds two-stage variants of those baselines and fine-tuned LLaVA-1.5-13B, Qwen2.5-VL-72B and LLaVA-OV-Qwen2-72B comparisons (Tables 8–9). New external comparisons include Gemini/GPT-based Self-Check and UniHD variants, plus HalLocalizer (Tables 4 and 10).

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce claim- and segment-level classification evaluation, zero-/two-shot Self-Check settings, category-specific HalLoc F1, two-stage and fine-tuned baseline controls, and alternative pruning settings. The original VisionHall training hyperparameters remain unchanged. The newly stated 400-sample test set and matched ablation training budget are disclosures, not demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained decoupling, backbone and few-shot ablations, v2 examines real-versus-synthetic span lengths and error frequencies, dependency-graph structure, and pruning sensitivity (Tables 2, 6–7). Tables 8–9 add controls investigating whether two-stage inference or fine-tuning alone explains the gains.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report experiments based on a single run. Neither provides repeated-seed estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty reporting. New descriptive dataset statistics do not change this practice.

E6.justification: The main VisionHall scores are retained, including ZINA's detection F1 of 45.15. v2 adds substantial result sets: MHaluBench segment-level macro-F1 is reported as 85.80 versus GPT-based UniHD's 81.71; pruning variants obtain detection F1 of 37.92 and 42.90 versus 45.15. HalLoc results favor ZINA in three categories but not Relationship, where it scores 0.64 versus HalLocalizer's 0.71. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under changed conditions.

T1.justification: The task definitions, tagging equations and span-metric formulas remain substantively unchanged. v2 adds explanatory formulas for existing CLIP-based metrics and conceptual dependency descriptions, but no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims about the fine-grained detection/editing task, ZINA and VisionHall remain. v2's conclusion expands the outperformance claim from VisionHall to VisionHall and MHaluBench; the principal method and dataset contributions are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations attributing gains to the combination of synthetic data and two-stage generation, interpreting pruning effects through dependency complexity, and explaining synthetic error-frequency differences. It also emphasizes preservation of unedited text and interprets external results as evidence of generalization. The original latency and underdetection limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the 400-sample VisionHall test set, original pruning probability p = 0.5, matched training budget for the single-stage ablation, and taxonomy-construction stages. Metric documentation is expanded. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, software tools, release licenses and project destination are retained, with much of their description relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused discussion of HalLocalizer and semantic-reconstruction work, distinguishing spans suitable for editing from token localization. It also adds image-editing, hallucination-snowballing and caption-metric references, while removing the opening survey discussion. This refines the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document: VisionHall becomes a standalone section, task and metric discussions gain explicit subsections, implementation details move to the appendix, and the introduction gains a contribution list. The appendices are reordered and expanded, and the evaluation and interpretation passages are rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven tables, retains and redistributes the four figures, changes the page template and caption placement, and reorganizes metric columns into Detection, Editing and Overall groups. The reordering introduces an error in Table 5: ZINA's final row retains the old numerical order under the new metric headings, contradicting Table 3 and the accompanying prose.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's VisionHall-only evaluation, v2 strengthens the empirical assessment through external benchmarks, two-stage and fine-tuned controls, and pruning analyses. However, new reporting errors limit the benefit: Table 5 misassigns ZINA's metric values, while Table 4 duplicates claim-level class scores that are incompatible with its reported macro-F1. The additional controls and documentation support a net improvement, but these inconsistencies prevent a clear major improvement.
